module: GE extension (core_camera, depends on core_vehicle_manager and core_environment): central manager of all the game's cameras. It loads the camera modes from the lua/ge/extensions/core/cameraModes folder (one file per mode), creates for each vehicle an instance of each mode (configured by the jbeam 'camera' section) and manages 'global' instances (free, observer, path, bigMap...) that exist once without a vehicle. It decides which camera is active (per player), handles the user configuration (camera order and activation, Options > Cameras menu, saved in the cameraConfig and freeCameraConfig settings), camera cycling (keys), transitions, and exposes the final position/orientation/FOV. The per-frame computation is in core/cameraUpdate.lua, the inputs in core/cameraInput.lua (re-exposed here). A modder uses it to read the camera position, change camera by name, drive the free camera or create extra views (contexts).
usage:
local pos = core_camera.getPosition()
local fwd = core_camera.getForward()
core_camera.setByName(0, 'orbit', true)          -- vehicle camera of player 0
core_camera.setByName('free')                    -- global camera
core_camera.setPosition(0, vec3(0,0,100))        -- only in free camera
notes: Choice of the active camera: if ctx.activeGlobalCameraName is set (global camera, e.g. 'free', 'observer', 'bigMap'), it is used; otherwise it is the player's vehicle camera 'focusedCamName' (among vdata.cameras, in the order of the 'configuration' list).

Contexts: one view = one context. 'main' is the player's view (RenderView 'main'); createContext adds extra views (split screen, video streams). Almost all get*(ctxId) functions take a context identifier (nil = main).

Per-vehicle functions (setRotation, setFOV, setOffset, setRef, setRefNodes, setTargetMode, setDistance, setMaxDistance, setDefaultDistance, setDefaultRotation, setSkipFovModifier, resetCameraByID, setup) always act on the main view and call the method of the same name on the active global camera or the vehicle's focused camera; if that camera lacks the method, nothing happens.

Per-player functions (setPosition, clearMotion, clearAngularMotion, setSmoothedCam, setNewtonRotation, setNewtonTranslation, resetCamera, hotkey) act on the player's view (pid); setPosition only positions the camera if the 'free' global camera is active.

Camera configuration: default list {orbit, driver, onboard.hood, external, relative, chase, droneChase}, replaced by the user setting cameraConfig if its version >= 2; the vehicle's other cameras are appended (sorted by the order field), 'occupant.*' cameras are inserted before 'onboard.hood'. A mode can have disabledByDefault = true.

The 'onboard' and 'occupant' mode types are 'multicam': the jbeam can define several entries, named '<mode>.<name>' (e.g. 'onboard.driver', 'occupant.xxx'). The legacy 'driver' mode is an alias of the 'occupant' constructor (constructorsCache.driver).
Modes marked isFilter (autopoint, autozoom, bobbing...) never become selectable cameras: they are created but ignored by initCam; other modes instantiate them to process their own result.
Cache: adding or removing a file in cameraModes (onFileChanged) invalidates the constructors and the caches of all contexts (hot reload).

Inconsistency: M.objectTeleported is assigned from the global objectTeleported defined in utils.lua (marked deprecated in the code: use objectTeleported directly). The automatic index wrongly reports this reference as undefined.
Inconsistency: setVehicleCameraByNameWithId uses the variable `player` (nonexistent in the function, so nil) in its error message.
Inconsistency: getCameraUnicycleZoom is local and not exported (only setCameraUnicycleZoom and unicycleZoomToggle are), unlike getCameraDriverZoom.
The extension replaces the global MoveManager with its own input table (newMove) and re-points it to the view being updated every frame.

speedFactor.desc: Speed factor (1 by default) used to correct a camera movement that is too slow/smoothed when creating thumbnails.

previousReplayStateName.desc: Last replay state seen by onReplayStateChanged (created on the fly).

objectTeleported.desc: Deprecated alias of the global objectTeleported (utils.lua).

setInputTargetPlayer.desc: Forces all camera inputs to target the given player (nil to disable this redirection).

getGlobalCameras.desc: Returns the name -> instance table of the global cameras (once per context, created on demand from the constructors where cam.isGlobal is true).

ctx.desc: Internal context (nil = main); external calls usually omit the argument

getGroupCams.desc: List of camera names of a group (e.g. 'world'), in the configured order. Disabled 'world' cameras are omitted unless includeDisabled is true (they remain visible in the options but are skipped when cycling).

getCameraGroups.desc: Sorted list of camera group names that have at least one usable camera.

nextCameraGroup.desc: Computes the next group in the cycle ring: game cameras (active = nil) to the first group, between groups, then from the last group to the game cameras (nil). active = false (system camera) returns nil.

active.desc: Active group: nil = game camera, false = camera without group

returns.desc: Next group or nil (back to game cameras)

getConfigurationReadOnly.desc: Deep copy of the vehicle camera configuration list ({name, enabled}).

getFreeCameraConfigurationReadOnly.desc: Deep copy of the configuration (order, activation) of the free cameras of the 'world' group.

displayCameraNameUI.desc: Sends the current camera name to the UI (Messages app) with the number of options and the current index. Does nothing for a unicycle (walking).

onCameraToggled.desc: Hook (emitted by cycleCameraGroup, setCameraByNameFromOptions): redisplays player 0's camera name.

notifyUI.desc: Notifies the UI and extensions of the camera change: guihooks 'onCameraNameChanged', hook onCameraModeChanged, then updates the options menu.

forcedCamName.desc: Name to announce instead of the focused camera

requestConfig.desc: Requests sending the current configuration to the Options > Cameras menu (guihooks CameraConfigChanged).

forcedCamName.desc: Camera name to mark as active

clearInputs.desc: Resets the rotation and zoom inputs (roll, pitch, yaw, zoom) of a MoveManager structure. Used by other GE scripts.

changeOrder.desc: Moves the camera at index camId by offset positions in the configuration list (skipping hidden cameras), then saves.

toggleEnabledById.desc: Enables or disables the vehicle camera at index camId in the cycle (compatibility) then saves the configuration.

changeFreeCameraOrder.desc: Moves a free camera in the 'world' cameras configuration and saves (freeCameraConfig setting).

toggleFreeCameraEnabledById.desc: Enables/disables a free camera of the 'world' group in the cycle and saves.

setGlobalCameraByName.desc: Activates a global camera by name, or switches back to the vehicle camera with nil. Calls onCameraChanged(false) on the old one and setCustomData + onCameraChanged(true) on the new one; in the main view, emits the onGlobalCameraSet hook. No effect if the name is unknown or if there is no vehicle to return to the vehicle camera.

name.desc: Global camera name, nil to leave

withTransition.desc: Not used in the code (inferred from code)

startCameraTransition.desc: Blends the current point of view into the camera's view for this frame. To call right after a camera change. duration overrides the configured duration.

cycleCameraGroup.desc: Switches to the next camera group (game cameras, then 'world' free cameras, then back), enters the first camera of the group, emits onCameraToggled and displays the name.

setByName.desc: Selects a camera by name. Flexible signature: setByName(player, camName, withTransition, customData) if the first argument is a number, otherwise setByName(camName, withTransition, customData). A global camera name (or nil) acts on the global view; otherwise it is the player's vehicle camera.

setCameraByNameFromOptions.desc: Selection from the Options menu: a 'world' group camera goes through enterGroupCam (and the onCameraToggled FreeCam hook), otherwise it is a vehicle camera. Displays the name if the selection succeeds.

setVehicleCameraByNameWithId.desc: Selects a vehicle camera for the vehicle with id vehId. If the vehicle data is not ready yet, the request is stored and applied later.

setBySlotId.desc: Selects the camera associated with a shortcut number (keys 1 to 9, slotId computed over the visible cameras).

setVehicleCameraByIndexOffset.desc: Switches to the next (offset = 1) or previous (-1) camera, skipping hidden/disabled ones. In a group's global camera, cycles within that group. Used by input actions.

isCameraInside.desc: Tests whether a camera position is inside the player's vehicle (within its oriented box and within 0.6 m of an 'inside' viewpoint of a camera).

returns.desc: 1 if inside, 0 otherwise (also 0 without a vehicle or on a unicycle)

getCameraDataById.desc: Returns the camera instances of a vehicle.

returns.desc: Cameras by name, nil if the vehicle is unknown

getDriverCameraNameById.desc: Name of the driver camera: 'driver' (if 'onboard.driver' exists) or the name of an 'occupant.*' camera in 'driver' permission mode.

getDriverDataById.desc: Driver camera data of a vehicle.

getDriverData.desc: Like getDriverDataById from a vehicle object.

getActiveCamName.desc: Name of the player's active camera: global camera if active, otherwise vehicle camera (or the pending requested one). nil if the player has no vehicle.

getActiveCamNameByVehId.desc: Name of a vehicle's focused camera (main view).

getActiveGlobalCameraName.desc: Name of the global camera active for the player, nil if it is a vehicle camera.

isWorldCamera.desc: Tests whether the player's active camera belongs to the 'world' group (free cameras).

processVehicleCameraConfigChanged.desc: (Re)creates the camera instances of a vehicle from its jbeam data (cameraData), updates the shared configuration (order, activation, saved by the main context), then chooses the camera: pending request, otherwise previous camera, otherwise first enabled and visible camera, otherwise first existing one. Returns false if the vehicle data is not available yet.

focusedCamNamePrevious.desc: Name of the previously focused camera

resetCameraByID.desc: Calls reset() on the camera (active global or the vehicle's focused one) of the main view.

setRotation.desc: Sets the camera orientation. If the 'free' global camera is active, also applies the rotation (quat) directly to the engine; then calls cam:setRotation(...).

setFOV.desc: Sets the field of view (degrees). If 'free' is active, also applies it to the engine; then cam:setFOV(...).

setOffset.desc: Delegates cam:setOffset(...) to the main view's camera.

setRefNodes.desc: Delegates cam:setRefNodes(...) (center, left, rear reference nodes).

setPosition.desc: Sets the camera position (vec3 as the first extra argument). If the 'free' global camera is active in the main view, the position is also applied directly to the engine; then cam:setPosition(...) is called.

clearMotion.desc: Cancels the movement (velocity) of the player's camera (cam:clearMotion).

clearAngularMotion.desc: Cancels the angular movement of the player's camera.

setNewtonRotation.desc: Enables/disables the 'Newton' (inertia) mode for free camera rotation.

setNewtonTranslation.desc: Enables/disables the 'Newton' (inertia) mode for free camera translation.

globalCameraFunction.desc: Calls the method functionName of a named global camera. Logs an error if the camera or the method does not exist.

proxy_Player.desc: Calls the method fct on player 0's active camera (global or focused).

vehicleCamerasFunction.desc: Runs a method on all cameras of a vehicle, in all contexts.

resetCamera.desc: Resets the player view's inputs, emits the onCameraReset hook and calls reset() on the active camera.

hotkey.desc: Forwards a shortcut key to the active camera (the mode's hotkey method).

resetConfiguration.desc: Clears the cameraConfig and freeCameraConfig settings and recomputes the configuration for all vehicles.

setFastSpeedModifier.desc: Enables the fast speed modifier (key) of the main view.

setPosRot.desc: Places the free camera at a position (and optional quaternion orientation). No effect if the free camera is not active.

setFreeCameraYawPitchRollDeg.desc: Orients the free camera (only active if the 'free' global camera is active) from yaw, pitch (positive = looking down) and roll in degrees; cancels the angular velocity.

getYawPitchRoll.desc: Yaw, pitch and roll of the main camera in one call.

setSpeed.desc: Sets the movement speed of the free camera.

getSpeed.desc: Movement speed of a context's free camera (30 by default).

changeSpeed.desc: Multiplies or divides the main view's camera speed by (1 + 0.2*|val|) depending on the sign, clamped between 2 and 100, and displays a message. Ignored if camera zoom is disabled in the editor.

setLookBack.desc: Enables/disables looking backward for the player.

getLookBack.desc: 'Look backward' state of the main view.

setCameraUnicycleZoom.desc: Sets the zoom of the walking camera (unicycle).

unicycleZoomToggle.desc: Toggles the walking camera zoom between 0 and 1.

driverZoomToggle.desc: Toggles the driver camera zoom between 0 and 1.

getPositionXYZ.desc: Final position as separate components (avoids allocation).

getUp.desc: Camera 'up' vector (z axis rotated by the orientation).

getRight.desc: Camera 'right' vector (x axis rotated by the orientation).

getForward.desc: Camera 'forward' vector (y axis rotated by the orientation).

getForwardXYZ.desc: Forward vector as separate components (uses a reused internal vec3).

getFovDeg.desc: Final field of view in degrees.

getFovRad.desc: Final field of view in radians.

createContext.desc: Creates (or updates) an extra camera context = a camera output with its own RenderView, reusing all camera modes. The identifier 'main' (or nil) returns the main context. The render target (resolution, texture) is managed by the caller. vehiclePlayer lets the view show another seat's vehicle while player only provides the input.

player.desc: Player/seat whose view follows the inputs (0 by default)

destroyContext.desc: Destroys an extra context (never the main one) and empties the main context's camera cache.

getContextIdForPlayer.desc: Identifier of the view through which this player looks, usable with the get*(ctxId) getters. nil = main view.

setContextCamera.desc: Selects a camera on a context without touching the player. camName nil or global camera name: global camera (initialized with the view's current pose); otherwise the vehicle camera of the context's player.

returns.desc: No useful return (the internal function returns nothing)

getContextCameraState.desc: Lightweight serializable (JSON) snapshot of a context's camera: name, world pose (pos, rot, fov) and the mode's own state (data, via cam:serialize) so it can be restored.

setContextCameraState.desc: Restores a context's camera from a getContextCameraState snapshot. A mode with deserialize restores its state; a free/global camera without deserialize is put back at the saved pose.

getContextCameraParams.desc: Adjustable settings of a context's active camera, for the camera control UI / video stream. Each mode provides its list via listParams; descriptors {key, title, kind ('range'|'bool'|'choice'|'slots'), type ('float'|'int'|'bool'|'enum'), value, icon, default, min, max, step, unit, options}.

setContextCameraParam.desc: Applies a setting to a context's active camera by delegating to cam:setParam(key, value, id).

onPreRender.desc: Hook called just before rendering: updates the camera (cameraUpdate.onPreRender), then displays the pending camera name after a vehicle change.

onTrigger.desc: Hook called by BeamNG triggers: if the subject is the player's vehicle (or the triggerOverride), 'enter' with cameraOnEnter switches to the 'observer' global camera pointing at this camera object, and 'exit' with cameraOnLeave leaves it. While a scenario is starting, the request is held until the 'running' state.

onSettingsChanged.desc: Hook called when settings change: applies free camera smoothing and propagates onSettingsChanged to all cameras.

onVehicleResetted.desc: Hook called when a vehicle is reset: propagates to the vehicle's cameras and resets the focused camera unless resetCameraOnVehicleReset is false or a global camera is active.

onVehicleSpawned.desc: Hook called when a vehicle is created: creates its camera data in each context.

onVehicleReplaced.desc: Hook called when a vehicle is replaced (new config): recreates its cameras.

onVehicleSwitched.desc: Hook called when the player switches vehicle: starts a transition (except for a global camera), propagates to the cameras and schedules the name display. Ignores players other than 0.

onDespawnObject.desc: Hook called when an object is deleted: removes its camera data if it is not a reload.

onVehicleDestroyed.desc: Hook called when a vehicle is destroyed: removes its camera data from all contexts.

onScenarioRestarted.desc: Hook called when a scenario restarts: propagated to all cameras.

onScenarioChange.desc: Hook called when the scenario state changes: propagated to the cameras; if a trigger was pending and the scenario goes to 'running', it is replayed.

onFileChanged.desc: Hook called when a file changes: adding/removing a cameraModes file invalidates the caches (hot reload).

onMouseLocked.desc: Hook called when the mouse is locked/unlocked: forwarded to the active camera (mouseLocked), except in free camera.

onClientPostStartMission.desc: Hook called after the level starts: delegated to core/cameraUpdate.lua.

onClientEndMission.desc: Hook called at the end of the level: detaches the camera from the 'main' RenderView to avoid a dead reference.

onSerialize.desc: Serialization hook before Lua reload: serializes the global and vehicle cameras, the active global camera, the last vehicle, the pending trigger and the camera requests.

onDeserialized.desc: Restore hook after Lua reload (merges the serialized state into the existing cameras).

onReplayStateChanged.desc: Hook called when the replay state changes: on leaving playback ('playback' to 'inactive'), empties the vehicle camera cache (vehicles deleted by the replay would otherwise be lost).
